subject.title: Config: scaffold compaction loop guard settings

question: Should OpenClaw reserve `agents.defaults.compaction.guard` now, or should loop-guard configuration stay under the existing loop-detection and canonical runtime-guard work?
rationale: The PR adds a public config/default surface without runtime behavior, and current main already has an overlapping post-compaction guard namespace, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent config contract.

options.title: Pause and reconcile the namespace
options.body: Keep this PR open but require maintainer direction that either folds the concept into existing loop-detection config or defines the permanent compaction-guard runtime contract before merge.

options.title: Sponsor the dormant scaffold
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly accept the compatibility cost of a reserved no-op config block, then require rebase and real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Replace with a fresh runtime PR
options.body: Close or supersede this branch after opening a narrower PR that implements approved runtime behavior and docs together.

recommendation.title: Pause and reconcile the namespace
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open but require maintainer direction that either folds the concept into existing loop-detection config or defines the permanent compaction-guard runtime contract before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The related issue history and merged adjacent guard PR point to steipete as the best available owner for the config/product-policy decision.
